title: Booleans
summary: The two truth values `true` and `false`. They drive every `if`, every loop condition, and every logical check.

details.heading: What produces booleans
details.body: Comparisons (`==`, `~=`, `<`, `>`), logical operators (`and`, `or`, `not`), and many Roblox checks like `player:IsA("Player")` or `CollectionService:HasTag(inst, "tag")`.

details.heading: Truthiness
details.body: In conditions, everything is truthy except `nil` and `false`. So `if 0 then` runs, `if "" then` runs, `if {} then` runs.

explanation.whatItIs: A boolean is a value that is either `true` or `false` — a yes/no switch. Booleans are what conditions are made of: `if isDoorOpen then` asks 'is this true?'.
explanation.whyItExists: Programs make decisions. Booleans are the smallest unit of decision: on/off, yes/no, pass/fail.
whenToUse: Flags that track state: `local hasKey = false` … `hasKey = true`
whenNotToUse: Don't compare with `== true` / `== false` when you can use the value directly: `if hasKey then` reads better than `if hasKey == true then`
Don't use numbers as booleans (`1`/`0`); unlike C, Luau's `0` is truthy
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
local isGameOver = false

if isGameOver then
    print("Stop!")     -- skipped: false
end

isGameOver = true

if isGameOver then
    print("Stop!")     -- now runs
end
```
tips: BoolValue objects in Roblox wrap a boolean in `.Value` — don't confuse the two (see gotchas)
commonMistakes: Writing `if x = true then` (assignment instead of comparison)
Expecting `0` or `""` to be falsy — they aren't in Luau
Testing a BoolValue Instance directly instead of its `.Value` property

examples.title: A boolean flag controlling behavior
examples.code:
local doorOpen = false

local function openDoor()
    doorOpen = true
end

local function tryWalkThrough()
    if doorOpen then
        print("You walk through.")
    else
        print("Bonk. The door is closed.")
    end
end

tryWalkThrough()   --> Bonk.
openDoor()
tryWalkThrough()   --> You walk through.
